facts.text: Port Clinton was named for New York governor De Witt Clinton, the mastermind behind the Erie Canal that linked the Midwest to New York.
Dubbed the Walleye Capital of the World, Port Clinton’s waters in Lake Erie’s western basin produce some of the most prolific walleye fishing.
Every New Year’s Eve, downtown Port Clinton throws a Walleye Drop, a fireworks display that celebrates its fishing heritage.
The Ida Rupp Public Library serves Port Clinton and extends its reach to Marblehead and Put‑in‑Bay through satellite branches.
Port Clinton sits at the mouth of the Portage River where it empties into Lake Erie, anchoring the city’s maritime identity.
As the principal city of its micropolitan area, Port Clinton lies roughly 34 miles southeast of Toledo, Ohio.
